source_text: Apollinem facitis citharaedum atque divinum. Primum de Maia natus in insula Delo, Oblata mercede postmodum structor, obsecutus Laomedonti regi Trojanorum muros eduxit. Locavitque sese, quem deum seducti putatis: Ossibus cujus amor Cassandrae flagravit, Subdole quem lusit virgo, falliturque divinus. Officio vervecis potuit scire bicordem. Repudiatus enim discessit inde divinus. Terruit hunc virgo specie, quam ille deberet. Illa prior quae debuerat deum amavisse, Lasciviens qui Daphnem sic coepit amare: Et tamen insequitur, dum vult violare puellam; Gratis amat stultus, nec potuit consequi cursu. Vel, si deus erat, occurreret illi per auras. Sub tectis illa prior venit, remansit que divinus. Fallit vos gens hominum, nam victu tristi fuerunt. Admeti pecora quoque pavisse refertur. Lusibus impositis dum mitteret discum in altum, Sublapsum non potuit retinere: prostravit amicum: Ultimus ille dies fuit Hyacinthi sodalis. Si divinus erat, mortem praescisset amici.
pass_a_gloss: You make Apollo a cithara player and divine. First born from Maia on the island of Delo, afterwards with a wage offered he followed as a builder, and having followed King Laomedon of the Trojans, he brought forth the walls. And he rented himself, whom you think is a god: his bones were inflamed with love for Cassandra, and the divine one was deceitfully played by the virgin, and was deceived. By the office of a shepherd he was able to know the two-hearted one. For the divine one departed, having been rejected from there. The virgin terrified him with her appearance, which he ought to have done. She, who first ought to have loved the god, was wanton, and he began to love Daphne in this way: and yet he pursues, while he wants to violate the girl; the foolish one loves gratuitously, and he was not able to attain by pursuit. Or, if he was a god, he would have met her through the air. The virgin came first under the roof, and the divine one remained. The human race deceives you, for they were of sad food. It is also reported that he pastured the flocks of Admetus. While he was sending the discus high, having imposed games, he was not able to retain the one who slipped: he struck down his friend: that was the last day of his friend Hyacinth. If he was divine, he would have foreknown the death of his friend.

pass_b_english: You make Apollo a cithara player and divine. First born from Maia on the island of Delos, afterward, with wages offered, he served as a builder; having obeyed King Laomedon of the Trojans, he raised the walls. And he hired himself out, him whom you think is a god: his bones burned with love for Cassandra, and the virgin deceitfully played the divine one, and he was deceived. By the office of a shepherd he was able to know the two-hearted one. For the divine one departed, having been rejected from there. The virgin terrified him with the appearance which he ought to have produced. She, who first ought to have loved the god, was wanton, and he began to love Daphne in this way: and yet he pursues, while he wants to violate the girl; the foolish one loves for nothing, and he was not able to overtake her by running. Or, if he was a god, he would have met her through the air. The virgin came first under the roof, and the divine one remained. The human race deceives you, for they lived on sad fare. It is also reported that he pastured the flocks of Admetus. While he was sending the discus high, having imposed games, he was not able to retain the one who slipped; he struck down his friend: that was the last day of his comrade Hyacinth. If he was divine, he would have foreknown the death of his friend.
